content:
The passage describes zamindars who could assert sovereignty by refusing to pay revenue to the Mughal Empire, implying that their power and autonomy stemmed from the Mughal revenue system. This system allowed local landholders (zamindars) to collect revenue and maintain local control, so withholding revenue was a direct challenge to Mughal authority.  

The option that best fits this context is **universal taxation**, because the Mughal Empire’s reliance on revenue collection from these local elites gave zamindars leverage—by controlling revenue, they could effectively challenge central power.  

Final answer: (B)
